persona: evaluator-fuzz: a careful engineer hardening an external-evaluator integration (one evaluation = one hour on the real problem) who wants to know exactly how evolvekit reacts to every evaluator misbehaviour
journey:
Started 16:55 by reading README.md, docs/new-experiment.md, AGENTS.md, the binpacking example files and every --help. Copied examples/binpacking (skeleton, evaluate.py, instances.py, fake_responses.yaml, evolvekit.yaml) into my scratch dir, pointed the two command stages at my own fuzz_eval.py (wraps the real evaluator; FUZZ_MODE / FUZZ_TARGET / FUZZ_STAGE / FUZZ_SEEDIDX / FUZZ_SCALE env vars select the misbehaviour; it logs its own PIDs), set generations: 2 and stage timeouts to 8 s. Preflight was clean at 16:57 and the first healthy run finished seconds later (fake provider, no keys needed). I never read evolvekit/*.py or tests/.

Then I ran the 16 cases, each as preflight (misbehave on the seed) plus a short run (misbehave on children or on a deterministic half of them), and inspected console output, status, leaderboard, runs.jsonl, archive.json, traces and work/. Crash / no file / bad JSON / string-null-bool KPI / missing interpreter / spaces / relative paths / non-writable dir / 50 MB stdout / non-UTF-8 stderr were all handled well: the run survives, the candidate gets failure_score and a specific message plus the stderr tail lands in runs.jsonl `last_failure`.

The bad news: a missing, NaN or +/-Infinity objective KPI silently scores -0.0 and goes to #1 under direction: minimize, and preflight calls it clean (same for a typo in evaluate.score.objective). With healthy costs above 1000 the documented default failure_score -1000 makes crashed candidates the "best", and they get bred from. A grandchild holding stdout makes evolvekit block far past the timeout (45 s on an 8 s timeout) and mislabels a successful evaluation as a timeout. Evaluator failures are invisible in console/status/leaderboard and nothing stops a run where every child crashes; breadth even grows. Rows are only written at generation end, the redirected console log stays empty, and a run killed during generation 1 can never be resumed (seed flagged as behavioural duplicate of itself, "fix the harness"). I killed only PIDs I started; a final process scan found none of mine left. The repo was not touched by me (git status shows a docs/mission/DECISION_LOG.md change from another job). Finished 17:14.

entries.title: Missing / NaN / Infinity objective KPI silently scores -0.0 and ranks #1 under direction: minimize; preflight says clean
entries.step: Case 4 and 5: evaluator writes valid JSON with other KPIs but without the objective named in evaluate.score (or with NaN / Infinity / -Infinity), healthy candidates have a large positive cost (FUZZ_SCALE=1000 -> ~5600-5900). Also tried a typo in evaluate.score.objective.
entries.command:
(cwd = scratch dir, PY = <repo>\.venv\Scripts\python.exe)
FUZZ_SCALE=1000 FUZZ_MODE=missing_obj FUZZ_TARGET=all $PY -m evolvekit preflight --config exp/fuzz.yaml
FUZZ_SCALE=1000 FUZZ_MODE=missing_obj FUZZ_TARGET=some $PY -m evolvekit run --config exp/fuzz.yaml --run-dir runs/04-missing-obj
$PY -m evolvekit leaderboard --run-dir runs/04-missing-obj
(same with FUZZ_MODE=nan|inf|neginf; and preflight/run with objective: excess_pctt in the config)
entries.observed:
preflight: 'stage proxy ok ... kpis : bins_used=237, excess_pct_pooled=7.23982, ...' (no excess_pct) -> 'verdict : clean (0 failure(s), 0 warning(s))', exit 0. With NaN it even prints 'excess_pct=nan' and still 'verdict : clean'.
run: 'gen 0  seed score=-5871' / 'gen 1  3 child(ren)  best=-0 ...' / 'seed score : -5871' 'best score : -0'.
leaderboard: '| 1 | g001-c0002 | 1 | -0 | -0 | 3,3 |', '| 2 | g002-c0006 | 2 | -0 | -0 | 0,0 |', '| 3 | g001-c0004 | 1 | -5619.86 |' ... seed '-5871' is #5. status: 'best : g001-c0002 rank=-0 score=-0'. g002-c0005 lineage shows it was bred from the KPI-less g001-c0002. runs.jsonl for nan/inf: '"excess_pct": NaN' / 'Infinity' / '-Infinity' with score -0.0, also rank #1; those tokens also land in archive.json and board.html (not strict JSON). Typo config: preflight 'verdict : clean', run 'gen 0 seed score=-0', every candidate -0, 'improvement : 0', exit 0.
entries.expected: A command stage whose output lacks evaluate.score.objective (or any weighted KPI), or whose objective is non-finite, is a stage failure ('objective KPI excess_pct missing/non-finite in <file>') scored failure_score. Preflight must fail (exit 2) when the seed does not emit the objective, and should print the seed's computed score so a -0 is visible.
entries.why_it_matters: A +Infinity or missing cost (the worst possible outcome of a solver that found nothing) becomes the best candidate of the run, is reported as a ~5871-unit improvement, wins its archive cell and is bred from. On an hour-per-evaluation problem I would spend days and real money optimising toward 'evaluator forgot to write the number', and the tool that is supposed to catch harness bugs says clean. README promises 'Every score is a finite float' but not that it is a meaningful one.
entries.suggested_fix: Validate after every command stage that the objective and every weights/penalties KPI is present and math.isfinite; otherwise fail the stage with a message naming the KPI. In preflight, fail on a missing objective, print 'score = ...' per stage, and cross-check config KPI names (objective, weights, penalties, descriptors) against what the seed emitted. Never serialise NaN/Infinity into runs.jsonl.

entries.title: Documented default failure_score -1000 outranks healthy candidates when cost > 1000: crashed candidates become 'best', displace the seed's cell and are bred from
entries.step: Case 4 (variant): healthy objective is a large positive cost (~5600-5900, minimize), half of the children crash with exit 1.
entries.command: FUZZ_SCALE=1000 FUZZ_MODE=exit1 FUZZ_TARGET=some $PY -m evolvekit run --config exp/fuzz.yaml --run-dir runs/04b-failscore-vs-bigcost ; $PY -m evolvekit leaderboard --run-dir runs/04b-failscore-vs-bigcost ; $PY -m evolvekit status --run-dir runs/04b-failscore-vs-bigcost
entries.observed: 'gen 0  seed score=-5871' / 'gen 1  3 child(ren)  best=-1000  cells=2' / 'breadth 3 held (improving, already at the floor of 3)' / 'best score : -1000'. Leaderboard: '| 1 | g001-c0002 | 1 | -1000 | -1000 | 3,0 |' '| 2 | g002-c0006 | 2 | -1000 | -1000 | 0,0 |' then healthy -5619.86, -5724.84, -5822.48, seed -5871 last. status: 'best : g001-c0002 rank=-1000 score=-1000'. Both -1000 rows have last_failure 'stage proxy: exit code 1 ... RuntimeError: FUZZ: solver licence server unreachable'. g002-c0005 and g002-c0007 list the crashed g001-c0002 as parent; crashed g002-c0006 sits in the seed's cell [0,0] with a higher fitness than the seed. Preflight on the healthy seed (score -5871) prints no warning about failure_score.
entries.expected: A failed evaluation can never outrank a successful one. Either failures are excluded from ranking/archive entirely, or failure_score is enforced to be worse than the seed (preflight failure: 'seed score -5871 is below evaluate.failure_score -1000').
entries.why_it_matters: Routing/scheduling costs are routinely in the thousands or millions (the repo's own pyvrp example quietly sets failure_score: -1000000000.0, so the authors know), but README, docs/new-experiment.md and the init template all show -1000.0 with no warning. A licence-server outage would turn into the run's 'best result' and the run then counts crashes as improvement, so patience never triggers.
entries.suggested_fix: Make failed candidates unrankable (sort key: failed last) instead of relying on a magic number; at minimum have load_config/preflight/run refuse to start when the seed's score <= failure_score, and document the constraint next to failure_score in the README, new-experiment.md and the init template.

entries.title: A run interrupted during generation 1 can never be resumed: seed is re-evaluated, flagged a behavioural duplicate of itself, and the run ABORTs with 'fix the harness'
entries.step: Killed my own run mid-generation-1 (seed already logged, children still evaluating), then re-ran the identical command in the same --run-dir as the docs instruct.
entries.command:
FUZZ_MODE=slow FUZZ_SLEEP=4 FUZZ_TARGET=children $PY -m evolvekit run --config exp/fuzz.yaml --run-dir runs/18-kill-resume --generations 1 &   # kill $! after 14 s
FUZZ_MODE=slow FUZZ_SLEEP=4 FUZZ_TARGET=children $PY -m evolvekit run --config exp/fuzz.yaml --run-dir runs/18-kill-resume --generations 1
FUZZ_MODE=ok $PY -m evolvekit run --config exp/fuzz.yaml --run-dir runs/18-kill-resume --generations 1   # second attempt
entries.observed: 'reclaimed a stale lock from dead pid 15436' / 'gen 0  seed score=-7.36178' / 'ABORT: seed failed evaluation - fix the harness before spending: behavioural duplicate of g000-c0001 at stage proxy' / 'stop reason : seed failed evaluation ...', exit 0. runs.jsonl now has g000-c0001 (healthy seed, -5.871) plus g000-c0002 'rejected: true, reject_reason: behavioural duplicate of g000-c0001 at stage proxy'. The second attempt with a perfectly healthy evaluator gives the identical ABORT and appends a third seed row. (A kill during generation 2 resumed fine: 'resumed 4 candidate(s) from runs.jsonl'.)
entries.expected: 'resumed 1 candidate(s) from runs.jsonl' and generation 1 starts again, as docs/new-experiment.md promises: 'Interrupted or halted runs resume cleanly in the same --run-dir'.
entries.why_it_matters: With an hour-long evaluator generation 1 lasts many hours, so it is the most likely place for a reboot, Ctrl-C or provider halt. The run dir is then permanently stuck, every attempt burns another seed proxy evaluation, and the message sends me debugging a harness that is fine.
entries.suggested_fix: On start, if runs.jsonl already contains a successful human-seed row, resume from it instead of re-evaluating; exempt the seed from the behavioural-duplicate filter; never phrase a novelty rejection as 'seed failed evaluation'.

entries.title: Stage timeout is not a wall-clock bound: a grandchild holding stdout makes evolvekit block until it exits, the process tree is not killed, and a successful evaluation is reported as 'timeout'
entries.step: Case 6: evaluator spawns a worker (subprocess.Popen inheriting stdout/stderr). Variant A: both hang. Variant B: evaluator writes a valid output file and exits 0 in 0.2 s but the worker lives on for 25 s. Stage timeout 8 s.
entries.command:
FUZZ_MODE=hang_grandchild FUZZ_SLEEP=45 FUZZ_TARGET=all $PY -m evolvekit preflight --config exp/fuzz.yaml
FUZZ_MODE=grandchild_holds_stdout FUZZ_SLEEP=25 FUZZ_TARGET=all $PY -m evolvekit preflight --config exp/fuzz.yaml
entries.observed:
A: 'stage proxy  FAILED  45.1s  (timeout 8s per run)' / 'failure : timeout after 8s' - wall clock 46 s, i.e. evolvekit waited until the grandchild's own sleep(45) ended; the grandchild was never killed.
B: 'stage proxy  FAILED  25.2s  (timeout 8s per run)' / 'failure : timeout after 8s' although the evaluator exited 0 after 0.2 s with a valid KPI file; wall clock 26 s.
(Plain hang without grandchild: 'FAILED 8.0s ... timeout after 8s', child PID gone - fine.)
entries.expected: At timeout the whole process tree is terminated (Windows Job Object / taskkill /T; POSIX process group) and evolvekit returns within ~timeout regardless of who holds the pipe. If the evaluator process itself has exited 0 and the output file is valid, the stage is a success no matter what a leftover worker does with stdout.
entries.why_it_matters: Real hour-long evaluators are wrappers around solver binaries or worker pools. A solver that wedges would hang the whole evolvekit run forever (README: 'The stage timeout is a hard kill') while continuing to hold CPU and licences; and in variant B the 'timeout after 8s' message would make me raise the timeout, which cannot help.
entries.suggested_fix: Launch evaluators in their own job/process group and kill the tree on timeout; read pipes with a bounded wait after the child exits (or redirect evaluator stdout/stderr to files in work/ instead of pipes); decide success from the child's exit status plus output file; report 'evaluator exited 0 but a descendant kept stdout open' distinctly.

entries.title: Evaluator failures are invisible in run output, status and leaderboard, and nothing stops a run in which every child fails - breadth even grows
entries.step: Case 11 (and 1, 2, 3, 16): seed fine, every child's evaluator exits 1; let the run go for up to 12 generations.
entries.command: FUZZ_MODE=exit1 FUZZ_TARGET=children $PY -m evolvekit run --config exp/fuzz.yaml --run-dir runs/11-all-children-fail --generations 12 ; $PY -m evolvekit status --run-dir runs/11-all-children-fail
entries.observed: Console never mentions a failure: 'gen 1  3 child(ren)  best=-5.871  cells=2  spent=$0.0016' ... 'gen 3  4 child(ren)' ... 'gen 7  6 child(ren)' 'gen 8  6 child(ren) best=-5.871 cells=3 spent=$0.1104' / 'stop reason : stop.patience reached: no improvement > 0.001 for 8 generation(s)' / 'spend : $0.1104 over 63 call(s), 152922 token(s)', exit 0. runs.jsonl: 9 of 9 evaluated children have last_failure 'stage proxy: exit code 1 ... RuntimeError: FUZZ: solver licence server unreachable'. status prints candidates/novelty/behavioural/near-dupes/best/spend - no failure count. The markdown leaderboard shows the rows as plain '-1000' with no marker or reason. The only place the error exists is the undocumented runs.jsonl field last_failure.
entries.expected: A per-generation note ('g001-c0002 FAILED at proxy: exit code 1 - RuntimeError: ...'), a 'failed: N (x crash, y timeout, z bad output)' line in the run summary/status/leaderboard, and a hard stop analogous to budget.max_consecutive_provider_errors (e.g. budget.max_consecutive_evaluator_failures, default 3) that halts with the evaluator's own message.
entries.why_it_matters: A broken licence server, full disk or OOM on my evaluator host would silently burn the whole LLM budget and days of evaluator wall clock; adaptive_children reads the crashes as a plateau and spends more (3 -> 6 children). README gives provider outages exactly this protection ('bred 22 children into a dead backend') but evaluator outages none.
entries.suggested_fix: Print failures in the generation log, count them in status/summary/leaderboard (flag rows like the '!' hold-out flag), add a consecutive-evaluator-failure stop that is on by default, and do not count failed evaluations toward adaptive-breadth growth.

entries.title: Crashed and timed-out candidates enter the MAP-Elites archive as cell elites and are used as parents
entries.step: Case 1/11/16: inspected archive.json and lineage after runs where children failed for infrastructure reasons (exit 1) or timed out.
entries.command: FUZZ_MODE=exit1 FUZZ_TARGET=children $PY -m evolvekit run --config exp/fuzz.yaml --run-dir runs/01-exit1-children ; then read runs/01-exit1-children/archive.json and runs.jsonl (same for runs/11-all-children-fail and runs/16-slow-some)
entries.observed: archive.json cells: '{"coord": [3, 0], ..., "elite": "g001-c0004", "fitness": -1000.0, "score": -1000.0, "occupants": 3, "children": 2}'; 'children': {'g000-c0001': 4, 'g001-c0004': 2}; leaderboard lineage 'g002-c0006 ... g001-c0004 < g000-c0001'. The run log counts it as coverage: 'cells=2'. In the 12-generation run 17 of 36 children were bred from parents whose evaluator had crashed. In runs/16-slow-some the full-stage-timeout candidate g001-c0002 became elite of cell [3,3] and parent of g003-c0010.
entries.expected: A candidate with no successful command stage has no measured behaviour and should not occupy a cell, count toward 'cells=', or be sampled as a parent (README says only stage 0 and the novelty filters reject, but it does not say failures become elites).
entries.why_it_matters: Every child of a never-evaluated parent costs an LLM call and, for me, up to an hour of evaluation, for a lineage whose fitness is a placeholder. When the failure is my infrastructure's fault the prompt even tells the model the parent 'failed', steering it away from code that may be fine.
entries.suggested_fix: Keep failed candidates in runs.jsonl but out of the archive/parent pool (or make it a config switch, default off); optionally let the evaluator signal 'infrastructure error - do not score' via a reserved exit code.

entries.title: preflight swallows the evaluator's stderr: a crashing seed shows only 'exit code 1'
entries.step: Case 1/10 in preflight: seed evaluator raises a Python exception with a full traceback on stderr.
entries.observed: 'stage proxy  FAILED  0.3s  (timeout 8s per run)' / '    failure : exit code 1' / 'FAILURE : stage proxy: exit code 1' / 'verdict : failures (1 failure(s), 0 warning(s))'. No stderr, no stdout, no command line, no path. The `run` path keeps the traceback in runs.jsonl last_failure, but preflight works in a temp dir with no run directory, so there is nowhere to look. `run` prints the same bare 'ABORT: seed failed evaluation - fix the harness before spending: stage proxy: exit code 1'.
entries.expected: The tail of the evaluator's stderr (the same ~2000 chars that `run` stores), the exact command line that was executed, and the cwd - preflight is the tool README tells me to use to debug the harness.
entries.why_it_matters: To find out why my evaluator fails under evolvekit I have to guess the expanded command and reproduce it by hand; with differences in cwd/env/interpreter ('python' resolved to the system 3.12, not the venv) that is exactly the class of bug preflight should expose.
entries.suggested_fix: Print the stderr tail, expanded command and cwd under 'failure :' in preflight and in the run's ABORT message; add --keep-temp to leave the preflight work dir behind.

entries.title: Completed evaluations are only written to runs.jsonl at the end of the generation; status shows nothing in flight
entries.step: Polled the run dir every 3 s during a generation with a slow (4 s) evaluator, ran `status` mid-generation, then killed my run mid-generation.
entries.command: FUZZ_MODE=slow FUZZ_SLEEP=4 FUZZ_TARGET=children $PY -m evolvekit run --config exp/fuzz.yaml --run-dir runs/17-persist-timing --generations 1 &  (poll: wc -l runs.jsonl; ls work/stage_out) ; $PY -m evolvekit status --run-dir runs/20-status-midrun (while running)
entries.observed: 't=3s rows=1 evaluator_calls=4 stage_out=3' ... 't=26s rows=1 evaluator_calls=9 stage_out=9' / 't=29s rows=4'. status mid-generation: 'candidates : 1 (0 rejected)' 'generations : 0' 'archive : no archive.json snapshot yet' 'llm calls : 4' - no hint that a run is active, which candidate/stage is evaluating or for how long. After killing a run at 7 completed evaluator calls: runs.jsonl still 1 row; usage.jsonl has the 4 LLM calls whose children are gone.
entries.expected: Each candidate's row (or a per-stage progress record) is appended as soon as its stage finishes, resume reuses finished stage outputs in work/stage_out, and status shows 'running: pid N, gen 1, g001-c0004 stage full seed 1, 00:42:10 elapsed'.
entries.why_it_matters: One generation on my problem is 3+ children x (proxy + seeds x full + hold-out) = many hours. Any interruption throws all of it away and re-pays the LLM calls, and during those hours the documented tools cannot tell me whether the run is alive or wedged.
entries.suggested_fix: Write a stage-level journal (append-only) as each evaluator call completes and reuse it on resume; have status read .lock and the journal to show liveness and the in-flight evaluation.

entries.title: `run` exits 0 on 'ABORT: seed failed evaluation'
entries.step: Case 10 and 14: seed evaluator crashes / interpreter missing; checked the process exit code for wrapper scripts.
entries.command: FUZZ_MODE=exit1 FUZZ_TARGET=seed $PY -m evolvekit run --config exp/fuzz.yaml --run-dir runs/10-seed-fails ; echo $?
entries.observed: 'gen 0  seed score=-1000' / 'ABORT: seed failed evaluation - fix the harness before spending: stage proxy: exit code 1' / 'stop reason : seed failed evaluation ...' then a full leaderboard and economics table for the one failed row; exit code 0. (preflight correctly exits 2; locked dir exits 3; unwritable dir exits 1.)
entries.expected: Non-zero exit (e.g. 2) and no leaderboard/economics boilerplate around the one line that matters.
entries.why_it_matters: My nightly wrapper gates on exit codes; a run that did nothing because the harness is broken looks identical to a successful run.
entries.suggested_fix: Return a distinct non-zero exit code for ABORT / halted-on-error stop reasons and document the run exit codes next to preflight's.

entries.title: Console output is block-buffered when redirected: the log file stays empty while the run works
entries.step: Ran `run ... > logs/x.log 2>&1 &` (how any multi-day job is launched) and looked at the log while it ran and after killing it.
entries.command: FUZZ_MODE=slow FUZZ_SLEEP=5 FUZZ_TARGET=children $PY -m evolvekit run --config exp/fuzz.yaml --run-dir runs/20-status-midrun --generations 1 > logs/20.log 2>&1 &  ; sleep 9; cat logs/20.log
entries.observed: logs/20.log is empty at t=9 s although the seed finished in <1 s ('gen 0 seed score=-5.871' only appears when the process exits). The log of the run I killed at t=14 s (logs/18a.log) is 0 bytes forever.
entries.expected: Each generation/ABORT line is flushed as it is printed.
entries.why_it_matters: With hour-long evaluations the log would stay empty for hours and lose everything on a crash - combined with status showing nothing in flight, there is no way to see progress.
entries.suggested_fix: print(..., flush=True) or sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True) in the CLI; mention PYTHONUNBUFFERED in the docs until then.

entries.title: No retry and no way to mark a failure as infrastructure: one transient failure on seed 1 of a seeds: 3 stage discards the finished seed-0 evaluation and scores -1000; message wording is confusing
entries.step: Case 9: full stage with seeds: 3, evaluator crashes only when --seed 1.
entries.command: FUZZ_MODE=exit1 FUZZ_SEEDIDX=1 FUZZ_STAGE=full FUZZ_TARGET=children $PY -m evolvekit run --config exp/fuzz-seeds3.yaml --run-dir runs/09-seedidx1  (preflight with FUZZ_TARGET=all)
entries.observed: preflight: 'stage full  FAILED  0.3s x2 seed(s)  (timeout 8s per run)' / 'failure : exit code 1 (on seed 1 of 2 run)'. run rows: 'g001-c0004 score=-1000.0 rank=-1000.0 pub=-6.936 stages=[static, proxy] last_failure: stage full: exit code 1 (on seed 1 of 2 run) ... RuntimeError ...'. Seed 0 of full was evaluated successfully for all 4 promoted children (work/stage_out/g001-c0004.full.seed0.json exists) but none of it is in the row; seed 2 never ran. Behaviour matches the README ('The first failing run ends the stage'), but 'seed 1 of 2 run' on a seeds: 3 stage reads like seeds=2.
entries.expected: For transient failures: an optional bounded retry per evaluator call (evaluate.retries: 1) or a reserved exit code meaning 'infrastructure failure - halt/retry, do not score'. Message: 'seed index 1 (2nd of 3 runs) failed; 1 run completed'.
entries.why_it_matters: At one hour per seed, a flaky licence checkout on the second seed throws away an hour of good data and permanently brands a possibly excellent candidate -1000 (and, per the archive entry, may still breed from it).
entries.suggested_fix: Add an opt-in retry and an 'evaluator-error' exit code convention that feeds a consecutive-failure stop; keep the partial seed KPIs on the row; reword the message.

entries.title: Evaluator failure contract is undocumented (exit codes, where stderr goes, cwd, env, retries, work/ layout); --candidate help points at the wrong directory
entries.step: Looked in README.md, docs/new-experiment.md, examples and --help for how evolvekit treats a failing evaluator and where to find its error afterwards.
entries.command: grep -n -i "last_failure\|stderr\|working dir\|cwd\|stage_out\|work/" README.md docs/new-experiment.md ; $PY -m evolvekit preflight --help
entries.observed: grep: no hits at all for last_failure, stderr, cwd or work/ (failure_score is mentioned once: 'a crash below stage 0 is evaluate.failure_score'). The README's run-directory inventory lists runs.jsonl, usage.jsonl, archive.json, scratchpad.md, .lock, traces/ but not work/candidates or work/stage_out. preflight --help says candidates are 'saved under a run's candidates/ directory'; the real path is <run-dir>/work/candidates/ ('ls runs/00-ok/candidates: No such file or directory'). --help for run/status/leaderboard shows no defaults for --config / --run-dir. I only learned by experiment that: the command runs with cwd = config dir, inherits my environment, 'python' is resolved on PATH (system 3.12 here, not the venv), non-zero exit / missing file / bad JSON / non-numeric KPI => failure_score, the last ~2000 chars of stderr are kept in runs.jsonl last_failure, stdout is discarded, nothing is retried.
entries.expected: A short 'When the evaluator misbehaves' section in README/new-experiment.md with a table (what happened -> score -> where the message is), plus cwd/env/interpreter resolution rules and the work/ layout; defaults shown in --help.
entries.why_it_matters: These are the first things an integrator with an expensive evaluator needs to know, and today they can only be reverse-engineered by fuzzing.
entries.suggested_fix: Add that section, document last_failure and work/, fix the --candidate help text to work/candidates/, add defaults to argparse help, and recommend an absolute interpreter path (or sys.executable substitution such as {python}) in commands.

entries.title: search.generations / --generations are per invocation: re-running the same command on a finished or halted run dir runs and bills N more generations; the gen line's spent= restarts per invocation
entries.step: Followed the README advice 're-run the same directory' with the identical command on a run that had already finished its 2 generations.
entries.command: cp -r runs/00-ok runs/22-rerun-finished ; FUZZ_MODE=ok $PY -m evolvekit run --config exp/fuzz.yaml --run-dir runs/22-rerun-finished
entries.observed: 'resumed 7 candidate(s) from runs.jsonl (4/16 cells occupied ...)' / 'gen 3  3 child(ren)  best=-5.61986  cells=4  spent=$0.0025' / 'gen 4  3 child(ren) ... spent=$0.0142' / 'stop reason : generations exhausted'. status afterwards: 'llm calls : 20' 'spend : $0.0176' (was 9 calls / $0.0034). The generation line's spent= ($0.0025) is lower than what the run dir had already spent ($0.0034) while 'economics cum=$0.0059' is cumulative.
entries.expected: Either search.generations is a total for the run dir (resume stops immediately with 'generations exhausted'), or the docs/--help say clearly it is 'N more', and spent= on the generation line is cumulative like every other figure.
entries.why_it_matters: After a halt I re-run the same command to finish the plan; instead I get (and pay for) the full plan again on top. Two spend figures with different bases on adjacent lines make it unclear which one budget.max_usd guards.
entries.suggested_fix: Treat generations as a run-dir total by default (add --more N for extension), or document it; make spent= cumulative and label per-invocation spend separately.

entries.title: Ledger writability is not checked up front: with a read-only runs.jsonl a resumed run pays for a generation of LLM calls, then dies on the first write
entries.step: Case 15: (a) run dir path is a file, (b) run dir with a deny-write ACL, (c) existing run dir whose runs.jsonl is read-only (attrib +R), then resume.
entries.command: attrib +R runs\15c-ro-ledger\runs.jsonl ; FUZZ_MODE=ok $PY -m evolvekit run --config exp/fuzz.yaml --run-dir runs/15c-ro-ledger --generations 4
entries.observed: (a) 'error: [WinError 183] Cannot create a file when that file already exists: ...15a-is-a-file' exit 1. (b) 'error: [WinError 5] Access is denied: ...\15b-readonly\traces' exit 1, nothing spent - both fine. (c) 'resumed 7 candidate(s) from runs.jsonl ...' / 'g003-c0008 duplicate after 2 attempt(s) ...' x3 / 'error: [Errno 13] Permission denied: ...\runs.jsonl' exit 1; usage.jsonl grew from 9 to 15 rows (6 billed calls) while runs.jsonl stayed at 7 rows, so the spend has no candidates attached.
entries.expected: Open runs.jsonl / usage.jsonl / archive.json for append at start-up (before the first LLM or evaluator call) and fail fast; on a write error mid-run, dump the pending rows to a fallback file.
entries.why_it_matters: On Windows an AV scanner, a sync client or an editor holding runs.jsonl is common; the same code path after an hour-long evaluation would lose that evaluation.
entries.suggested_fix: Writability probe at start; catch OSError around ledger appends, retry briefly, then write to <run-dir>/runs.jsonl.pending and halt with a clear message.

entries.title: Em dash in the ABORT / stop-reason message is emitted as cp1252 byte 0x97 when output is redirected on Windows
entries.step: Read the redirected run log of a seed failure.
entries.command: FUZZ_MODE=exit1 FUZZ_TARGET=seed $PY -m evolvekit run --config exp/fuzz.yaml --run-dir runs/10-seed-fails > logs/10-seed-fails.run.log 2>&1 ; grep ABORT logs/10-seed-fails.run.log | od -c
entries.observed: 'ABORT: seed failed evaluation \227 fix the harness before spending: stage proxy: exit code 1' (od shows octal 227 = 0x97); renders as 'evaluation ? fix' / mojibake in UTF-8 viewers and CI logs.
entries.expected: ASCII ('--') or UTF-8 output regardless of the console code page.
entries.why_it_matters: It is the single most important line of a failed run and it is the one that gets garbled; grep/log shippers expecting UTF-8 choke on it.
entries.suggested_fix: Use ASCII punctuation in CLI messages or reconfigure stdout/stderr to UTF-8 with errors='replace'.

entries.title: 'rejected: N (x no-op, y duplicate, z behavioural)' does not add up: static rejects and unappliable responses are counted in N but not in the breakdown
entries.step: Read the run summary of the 8-generation all-children-fail run and tried to reconcile the numbers.
entries.command: FUZZ_MODE=exit1 FUZZ_TARGET=children $PY -m evolvekit run --config exp/fuzz.yaml --run-dir runs/11-all-children-fail --generations 12 ; $PY -m evolvekit status --run-dir runs/11-all-children-fail
entries.observed: 'rejected : 27 (8 no-op, 14 duplicate, 0 behavioural)'; status 'candidates : 37 (27 rejected)'. Counting reject_reason in runs.jsonl: 14 duplicate, 8 no-op, 2 "forbidden import(s): ['os']", 3 'could not apply response: ...' - the last 5 appear nowhere in the breakdown, and the 9 evaluator failures appear nowhere at all.
entries.expected: A breakdown that sums to N (add 'static' and 'unappliable'), plus the separate failed-evaluation count.
entries.why_it_matters: When auditing where a budget went, numbers that do not reconcile make me distrust the rest of the accounting.
entries.suggested_fix: Add the two missing categories to the summary/status/leaderboard line.

unanswered_questions: While a generation is in flight: which candidate / stage / seed index is being evaluated right now, since when, and how many evaluator calls of this generation have completed? (status shows 'generations : 0' and nothing else until the generation ends)
Is a run currently alive on this run dir? status does not show the .lock owner pid or whether it is still running.

How many candidates failed evaluation in this run, split by crash / timeout / bad output and by stage? No documented tool reports it; I had to parse runs.jsonl for the undocumented last_failure field.
Where are my evaluator's stdout and stderr for a SUCCESSFUL evaluation, and the full stderr of a failed one? As far as I can tell stdout is discarded and only the last ~2000 chars of stderr survive.
Can candidates that failed for infrastructure reasons be re-evaluated after the harness is fixed, without paying the LLM again? Are the finished files in work/stage_out ever reused on resume?
Can the evaluator signal 'infrastructure failure - halt or retry, do not score this candidate' (reserved exit code)? Is there any evaluator retry setting?
Do budget.max_usd / max_tokens / max_full_evals_per_day count across resumed invocations or per invocation? The generation line's spent= restarts at each invocation while cum= does not.
Is search.generations a total for the run dir or 'N more per invocation'? (Observed: N more; undocumented.)

What are the evaluator command's cwd, environment and interpreter resolution, and is it run through a shell? (Observed: cwd = config dir, env inherited, 'python' taken from PATH = system Python rather than the venv; undocumented.)
Are evaluator calls ever run concurrently, and can I ask for that (or forbid it)? Observed strictly sequential; nothing in the docs either way.
What are the defaults for --config and --run-dir? --help lists the flags with no defaults or descriptions.
Does the HTML dashboard still render when runs.jsonl contains NaN/Infinity tokens? (board.html embeds a bare NaN; I did not open it in a browser.)
After a full-stage timeout the row keeps public_score = the proxy score but score/ranking_score = -1000: which of these do parent sampling and the archive use?
went_well: Time to first run of my own experiment was about 2 minutes: copying examples/binpacking as docs/new-experiment.md suggests, swapping the command and running preflight/run with the fake provider just worked, from any cwd.

Exit 1 with traceback, exit 0 with no output file, invalid JSON, and objective as string / null / boolean are all handled: the run survives, the candidate gets failure_score, and the message is specific, e.g. "evaluator wrote no output file at g001-c0002.proxy.json", "evaluator output was not readable JSON: Expecting property name ... line 1 column 30", "KPI 'excess_pct' was '5.871'; KPIs must be numbers or lists of numbers".
On failure the TAIL of stderr (about 2000 chars, so the actual exception rather than the banner) is stored in runs.jsonl last_failure; a 60,000-line stderr did not bloat the ledger.
A failing seed aborts the run before any LLM call is made ('ABORT: seed failed evaluation - fix the harness before spending'), and preflight returns exit 2 for the same condition.
Re-running the same run dir after fixing a seed failure re-evaluates the seed cleanly and carries on.

A plain hang is killed at exactly the stage timeout ('FAILED 8.0s ... timeout after 8s'), the evaluator PID is really gone afterwards, the run continues, and the timeout is reported to the next prompt for that parent. An in-flight evaluator also did not outlive an evolvekit process that I terminated.
50 MB of evaluator stdout: no deadlock, no memory or disk bloat, stage only ~0.8 s slower.
Non-UTF-8 bytes on stderr: no crash in run, status, leaderboard or --html; bytes are replaced with U+FFFD in last_failure.

Spaces in the run dir and in the config dir both work; a relative --run-dir resolves against the cwd and the evaluator receives absolute {candidate}/{out} paths, so running from another directory works.
A nonexistent interpreter gives a clear, actionable message: "could not run 'python3.99-nope': [WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified".
A run dir that is a file or is not writable fails immediately with exit 1 before anything is spent.
The run lock works as documented: second run refused with exit 3 and a message naming the pid and start time; a stale lock from a killed run is reclaimed automatically.
seeds: 3 behaves as documented: the stage stops at the first failing seed and the failure names the seed index; per-seed output files are kept in work/stage_out.
preflight --candidate works on a saved candidate file and gives timeout advice on a realistic candidate.
